_schema.note: Each category's 'resources' array holds objects with this shape. Filling the directory is just adding objects here — no other file needs to change.

resource.name: string — resource name
resource.type: string — one of: website, tool, guide, dataset, organization, publication

resources.name: Consumer Federation of America
resources.description: A nonprofit association of consumer groups that has advocated for US consumers since 1968. Publishes research, tips and policy analysis on banking fees, credit, debt collection and financial products.

resources.name: National Consumer Law Center
resources.description: Nonprofit consumer law experts working on behalf of low-income consumers. Their free consumer-facing resources explain debt collection, credit reporting, student loans and what to do when a lender breaks the rules.

resources.name: National Foundation for Credit Counseling (NFCC)
resources.description: The largest US network of nonprofit credit counseling agencies. Its agency finder connects people with accredited counselors for budgeting and debt management plans, as an alternative to for-profit debt relief companies.

resources.name: r/personalfinance Wiki
resources.description: Community-maintained wiki from one of the largest personal finance forums online. Known for its step-by-step 'what to do with my money' flowchart, plus plain guides on debt, banking and building credit.

resources.name: StepChange Debt Charity
resources.description: UK charity offering free, confidential debt advice online and by phone, including an online debt tool that builds a personal action plan and debt solutions without fees.

resources.name: Which? Money
resources.description: The money section of Which?, the UK's consumer association. Independent guides on bank accounts, savings, credit and scams, with practical advice on complaining and getting money back.

resources.name: Better Finance
resources.description: The European federation of investors and financial services users. Independent research and campaigns on banking fees, retail investment products and pensions from the consumer side.

resources.name: Financial Rights Legal Centre
resources.description: Australian community legal centre that helps people with debt, credit, banking and insurance problems. Free fact sheets, sample letters and a national helpline.

resources.name: United Policyholders
resources.description: Nonprofit that helps policyholders navigate insurance claims, especially after disasters. Free claim guides, sample letters, a 'Roadmap to Recovery' program and practical tips for resolving disputes with insurers.

resources.name: Consumer Watchdog
resources.description: California-based nonprofit consumer group with a long track record on insurance rates and practices. Publishes investigations, consumer alerts and case updates on insurer conduct.

resources.name: Citizens Advice – Insurance
resources.description: Free, step-by-step guidance from the UK charity on what to do when an insurer refuses or delays a claim, how to complain, and when to escalate to the Financial Ombudsman.

resources.name: Resolver
resources.description: Free online tool that helps you raise and track complaints with insurers and other companies, keeps all correspondence in one place and guides you through escalation if the company doesn't respond.

resources.name: Fairer Finance
resources.description: Independent UK consumer group that rates insurers and banks on customer experience and policy quality, and publishes a regular Trust in Insurance Index. Useful for comparing how insurers actually treat customers.

resources.name: CHOICE – Insurance advice
resources.description: Guides from Australia's leading independent consumer organisation on choosing insurance, understanding exclusions and what to do when a claim goes wrong.

resources.name: Consumer Action Law Centre
resources.description: Australian community legal centre with free fact sheets and toolkits on insurance disputes, unfair claims handling and consumer rights, plus a free legal advice line for Victorians.

resources.name: Web3 is Going Just Great
resources.description: An independent, sourced timeline of crypto scams, hacks, rug pulls and collapses, with a running total of losses. A sober reality check before putting money into any crypto project.

resources.name: Citation Needed
resources.description: Independent newsletter and podcast by Molly White, the researcher behind Web3 is Going Just Great. Clear, well-sourced analysis of crypto, fintech and the policies around them, written for non-specialists.

resources.name: Chainabuse
resources.description: Free community database of reported crypto scams. Search a wallet address, website or domain to see if others have reported it, or file your own report to warn people.

resources.name: Revoke.cash
resources.description: Free, open-source tool to see and cancel the token approvals your crypto wallet has granted. Its learning section explains in plain language how approval scams drain wallets and how to protect yourself.

resources.name: Global Anti-Scam Organization (GASO)
resources.description: Volunteer-run nonprofit founded by scam survivors. Supports victims of romance and crypto investment scams ('pig butchering'), publishes scam reports and warns about fake 'fund recovery' services.

resources.name: Operation Shamrock
resources.description: Nonprofit coalition fighting pig-butchering and crypto investment scams. Its library and podcast explain how these scams work, who runs them and what victims can do.

resources.name: AARP – Cryptocurrency Scams
resources.description: Plain-language guide from AARP's Fraud Watch Network on how crypto scams work, including crypto ATM and romance scams, and the warning signs to share with older relatives.

resources.name: NCLC – Payments & Payment Fraud
resources.description: Resources from the National Consumer Law Center on payment apps like Zelle and Cash App, prepaid cards and fintech accounts. Explains which protections you have when money is stolen or sent to a scammer.

resources.name: LawHelp.org
resources.description: Run by the nonprofit Pro Bono Net, it connects people with free legal aid organizations in their state and offers plain-language guides on consumer, housing, debt and family law problems.

resources.name: Wex – Legal Information Institute (Cornell)
resources.description: Free, collaborative legal dictionary and encyclopedia from Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute. Clear definitions of contract and consumer-law terms you'll meet in agreements and disputes.

resources.name: Terms of Service; Didn't Read
resources.description: Community project that reads and grades the terms of service and privacy policies of popular websites and apps, highlighting the clauses that matter. Also available as a browser extension.

resources.name: Upsolve
resources.description: Nonprofit that offers a free online tool to file Chapter 7 bankruptcy without a lawyer for people who qualify, plus a large library of plain-English guides on debt, collections and lawsuits.

resources.name: CourtListener
resources.description: Free, nonprofit legal search engine from the Free Law Project. Search millions of court opinions and federal court records, and set alerts on cases you're following.

resources.name: Which? Consumer Rights – Template Letters
resources.description: Free template letters from the UK consumer association for complaints, refunds, faulty goods, cancelled contracts and compensation claims, each with guidance on your legal rights.

resources.name: Advicenow
resources.description: Run by the charity Law for Life, it publishes independent, practical guides to help people in England and Wales understand and deal with legal problems on their own, from disputes to tribunals.

resources.name: LawWorks
resources.description: Charity that connects people who can't afford a lawyer with free legal advice clinics across England and Wales, staffed by volunteer lawyers.

resources.name: Justice Connect
resources.description: Australian not-for-profit providing free legal help and plain-language self-help resources, including support for people facing debt, bankruptcy and unfair contracts.
